data.name: Madelene
data.gender_notes: Madelene is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, Mary Magdalene is a woman from Magdala, a town on the shores of the Sea of Galilee, who was a follower of Jesus. She is known as the 'apostle to the apostles' because she was the first person to see the resurrected Jesus and share the news of his resurrection with the disciples. Her name 'Magdalene' is derived from 'Makrina' or 'Margarita', meaning 'pearl' or 'gems of the sea', reflecting her value as a precious disciple and witness to Jesus' resurrection.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes faith and devotion to Jesus and the Christian message.
data.etymology: Madelene belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gem of the sea.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Madelene total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: מדלין
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מדלין נגזר מהמילה העברית 'מדל' שפירושה גדולה או מרוממת. הוא קשור לנושא הרוממות והגדילה של האל. השם קיים גם בברית החדשה ומשמש כסמל לאישה שמרוממת ומעלה את האל.

in_greek.name: Μαδελίνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μαδελίνη προέρχεται από το ελληνικό χωριό Μάγδαλα και σχετίζεται με την Μαρία η Μαγδαληνή, μια από τις σημαντικότερες προσωπικότητες της Καινής Διαθήκης. Ονομάζεται έτσι λόγω της καταγωγής της από το χωριό Μάγδαλα και συμβολίζει την πνευματική ανάσταση και τη σχέση με τον Ιησού Χριστό.

in_latin.name: Magdalena
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Madelene is derived from the Latin 'Magdalena', which means 'elevated' or 'tower'. It is associated with Mary Magdalene, a key figure in the New Testament. The name signifies spiritual elevation and a strong connection to Christian tradition and faith.

in_english.name: Madelene
in_english.long_meaning: The name Madelene originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, meaning 'tower', 'elevated', or 'great'. It is associated with Mary Magdalene, a significant figure in the New Testament. The name symbolizes spiritual elevation, greatness, and a strong connection to Christian faith and tradition. It has been used across various Christian cultures, signifying a person of great spiritual significance and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Madelene" has been deeply embedded in Western culture through its association with Mary Magdalene, one of Jesus' most beloved and intriguing disciples. Her image as a penitent sinner, transformed by the love of Christ, has been depicted in art and literature throughout history. The name has been given to girls to signify their worth and value as a precious creation, and it continues to be a popular name today.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Madelene" holds a deep spiritual significance for Christians, as it is a reminder of the transformative power of God's love. Mary Magdalene's story of redemption and faith in the face of adversity is a source of inspiration and hope for many. Her name serves as a reminder that no matter what our past mistakes or sins may be, we can always turn to God for forgiveness and new beginnings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mary Magdalene: A symbol of redemption and transformation. Her tears represent sorrow for past mistakes, while the alabaster jar of expensive perfume signifies the cost of true repentance and love. In Christianity, she is revered as the first witness to the resurrection of Jesus Christ.

biblical_reference.note: The name is associated with Mary Magdalene, a follower of Jesus Christ and the first to witness His resurrection.

historical_references.reference: Mary Magdalene is believed to be the unnamed woman who anointed Jesus' feet with expensive perfume in Luke 7:36–50. The woman is also described as a sinner in Luke 7:37, a description which has led to the identification of Mary Magdalene with the repentant sinner in Luke 7:36–50, and with the unnamed woman in Luke 21:1–4, who also anointed Jesus' feet.

The legend of Mary Magdalene as a penitent sinner and the apostle to the apostles may have developed in the 6th century AD. According to this legend, after Jesus' crucifixion, Mary Magdalene went to the Holy Land and became a follower of Jesus' brother James, the Just, in Jerusalem. She is said to have preached the gospel in Southern France and Provence, where she is venerated as the patron saint of the region.
historical_references.context: Emergence of Mary Magdalene as a venerated figure in Christian tradition
